question: What necessary codebook-size bound follows for any actually used multi-sign entry of an arbitrary finite prefix-free word-preserving letter code, allowing shared initial signs?
contract: One fixed finite prefix-free table C of distinct nonempty words over the22working units. Arbitrary finite lengths and several entries per head allowed. Every unchanged eligible whole group belongs to C*. Nontrivial requires an actually consumed code of length>1. Identity always covers W and is not a nontrivial positive. No source values, contextual spelling, optional errors, nulls or moved word boundaries.
selection: All and only immutable1233GROUPS, separately by reader. No new query, native image, word selection or normalization. Every occurrence retained; deduplicate only mathematical constraints.
algorithm: Iteratively add nonempty left prefix quotients: u,v=u r in R implies r. Save earlier parent IDs for every new string. Full fixed point required; otherwise UNKNOWN. Compute H first signs, F singleton strings, T two-sign edges, d distinct second signs. For every occurring possible long-code head g including g outside H, compute N backwards-reachable in T. If N intersects F g impossible. Otherwise direct bound |H union {g}|+max(1,d_g)-1 and stronger |H union {g}|+sum(max(1,d_h)-1 for h in N). Minimum remaining bound is necessary only, never exact minimum. Also compute irreducible prefix basis P for exact constraint reduction; it is a native-fitted formal code, not source language or a human writer.
cap_meaning: Generic cardinality reference points only, not particular source alphabets. Report excluded only if necessary bound exceeds cap; otherwise NOT_EXCLUDED. If all heads forced singleton, no nontrivial code at any size. No solver follows a non-exclusion.
